anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer repeatedly chooses a substantially sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are adequate.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume nearly all available CPU cycles, creating system-wide compute saturation.

Composite definition: The database simultaneously suffers from poor plan selection that drives excessive instruction work and a host-level CPU bottleneck that throttles every session. 

Combined phenomena: 1) Identical statements oscillate between index and full-scan plans, or lock into an inefficient nested-loop plan, while overall CPU usage stays pegged near 100 %. 2) Top SQL lists are dominated by the mis-planned statements, but even unrelated workloads show rising latency because runnable queues grow and OS context switches spike. 3) Wait-event views display a mixture of CPU-scheduler waits and execution-engine waits (e.g., latch or buffer-access) caused by the bad plan, making diagnosis ambiguous. 4) Any plan cache invalidation, statistics refresh, or parameter change can trigger another flip to a different—but still CPU-hungry—plan, producing saw-tooth performance patterns during peak load.

Causal chain: A sub-optimal plan (e.g., non-selective full table scan or parallel-degree overuse) multiplies the required CPU instructions per request. The extra CPU demand quickly exhausts core capacity, pushing the system into saturation. Once CPU queues lengthen, task scheduling delays inflate query runtimes further, feeding back into the optimizer’s adaptive thresholds; this may cause additional plan re-compiles or parallel downgrade/upgrade decisions, perpetuating unstable plan choices. Conversely, chronic CPU pressure can keep apparently cheap but actually expensive plans in cache because re-optimization is deferred, thereby locking the workload into a high-CPU state. The intertwined effects of bad plans producing CPU spikes and CPU starvation masking or reinforcing those plan flaws amplify overall performance degradation and hinder straightforward root-cause isolation.

entry.official_definition: The execution timeout for SELECT statements, in milliseconds.
entry.trigger_condition: A SELECT statement exceeds the configured max_execution_time limit.
entry.workload_impact: The SELECT statement is interrupted by the execution time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
